learningObjectives: Distinguish message controls from tabs in current API Scan documentation.
Inspect actual response data without treating it as an automatically correct expected result.
Apply an independent contract-scoped create/read verification workflow.
Add multipart file parts using documented attachment controls.

rows: HTTP request-method selector; not a payload tab.
API base URL and resource identifier.
Edit the payload of the selected message.
Edit parameters according to the service contract.
Configure authentication and advanced message settings.
Inspect request or response headers according to the selected view.

elements.title: File parts and request/response views
items: For a non-multipart message, use Home > Add Files > Attachment to add a file part and switch to Multipart View.
For an existing multipart message, Add Files is disabled. Use Toggle Multipart as needed, then Add Part > Link To File or Enter Content; inspect each part name, Content-Type and headers.
Use Home Request and Response to inspect the selected message view. Attachments are not described as a universal standalone Attachments tab in the current workflow.

elements.text: Running a message can reveal actual behavior, generated identifiers and integration errors. Independent guidance: compare these observations with the contract; do not copy observed values into expected results as proof they are correct. A successful status still needs business assertions.

bulletPoints: Method, Endpoint and Resource are controls, not three payload tabs.
Inspect part metadata and actual response evidence; avoid making the current response its own unexamined oracle.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Independent example: create and verify a shop

elements.title: Use the documented sandbox contract
items: Assume the authorized sandbox defines GET /shops for a collection and POST /shops for creation; configure credentials as its contract requires.
Retrieve and inspect the current collection, including pagination/filtering rules; do not assume it is always a complete list.
Send a valid creation request and inspect its status, response body and resource identifier. 201 or another documented success response may apply; 200 alone does not prove persistence.
Retrieve the created resource by identifier, or inspect the collection according to the contract, and assert the expected fields.
Avoid depending on insertion order; record identifiers and clean up created test data where the sandbox workflow permits it.

elements.text: Payload fields are API data. They are not automatically Tosca Reusable TestStepBlock Business Parameters; exported Module Attributes and assertions are configured separately.

bulletPoints: Verify identity and expected fields; do not depend on a new entry being last in a response list.
Preserve payload data types and valid syntax according to the selected format and contract.

elements.text: Use an authorized disposable sandbox to configure a creation request, inspect its response and retain the created identifier. Original Academy video/exercise files are inaccessible and uncertified.

Retrieve the created resource and compare its fields to independently defined expected values. Check negative behavior and cleanup requirements from the contract. This is independent guidance, not a verified Academy exercise solution.

examPitfalls.title: Confusing controls with tabs
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Treating Method, Endpoint and Resource as payload tabs or looking for the HTTP method inside the body.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Method is a selector; Payload contains body data. Params, Auth and Advanced are documented tabs, with Headers as a section.

examPitfalls.title: Using the current response as its own test oracle
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Copying server output into expected values without validating it against the contract.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Inspect observations, identifiers and errors, but define correctness from business requirements and explicit assertions.

examPitfalls.title: Ignoring payload syntax, types and contract
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Changing body values without preserving the intended data types or required structure.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Use valid syntax for the chosen format and the service contract; not every JSON value is a quoted string.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which API Scan message control selects the HTTP method used by the request?
practiceQuiz.hint: The current docs distinguish controls from tabs.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Method selects the HTTP request method; Payload is body content and Resource is a resource identifier.

optionExplanations.A: Payload holds body data, not the method selector.
optionExplanations.B: Method is the documented selector for the HTTP request method.
optionExplanations.C: Resource identifies the requested resource rather than choosing the method.
optionExplanations.D: An attachment path identifies a file, not the HTTP method.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A non-multipart message needs to include an image file as an attachment part. Which current documented workflow adds it?

options.text: Put the file path in Params and assume it uploads.
Change Endpoint to the image filename.
Use Add Files > Attachment, then inspect the new multipart part properties.

practiceQuiz.hint: The scenario starts with a message that is not already multipart.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Add Files > Attachment adds the selected file as a part and switches to Multipart View. For already multipart messages the button is disabled; use Add Part instead.

optionExplanations.A: A parameter containing a path does not automatically attach file content.
optionExplanations.B: Changing the API base URL does not add a file part.
optionExplanations.C: This is the documented route for the stated initial message type.
optionExplanations.D: Renaming the resource identifier does not add an attachment.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Why can running a message in API Scan before export be useful?

options.text: Every message must run once before export is technically permitted.
It reveals actual behavior and identifiers to compare with the contract and explicit expected results.
Exporting first is always faster, so inspection is useless.

practiceQuiz.hint: Observe behavior without assuming current output is correct.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Running messages provides response evidence and can reveal integration issues. Validate it against requirements; it does not make every observed value a correct expected value.

optionExplanations.A: A universal run-before-export prerequisite is not established by the accessed docs.
optionExplanations.B: Observed behavior can inform testing when checked against independent expectations.
optionExplanations.C: The documented API tooling supports API test construction.
optionExplanations.D: This universal performance claim does not justify skipping useful inspection.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A sandbox contract exposes a shop collection for retrieval via GET. Which method should be used for that read operation?
practiceQuiz.rationale: GET requests a selected representation. Inspect pagination and filtering for list completeness; safe method intent does not prohibit incidental server logging.

optionExplanations.A: GET matches the stated retrieval operation and HTTP read intent.
optionExplanations.B: POST asks for resource-specific processing and is not this stated read operation.
optionExplanations.C: PUT requests target-state creation or replacement.
optionExplanations.D: DELETE requests removal of the target mapping, not collection retrieval.

quickRecap.value: Method / Endpoint / Resource controls; Payload / Params / Auth / Advanced tabs; Headers section.
Inspect body syntax and types against the service contract.
Non-multipart: Add Files > Attachment; existing multipart: Add Part and inspect part metadata.
Evidence to compare with requirements, not automatically correct expected values.
Use contract-specific methods and created identifiers; assert fields without assuming list insertion order.
